reasoning_content:
I'm noticing that `terms_data_protection` and the other terms fields aren't database columns, but the setter methods still work because the custom User model must be defining `attr_accessor` for them somewhere. That's why assignments succeed without raising an error, and the user passes validation because the acceptance validation on `terms_data_protection` is satisfied.

The real problem is that `terms_of_service` doesn't have an accessor defined at all, so it throws a NoMethodError. The cleanest fix is to strip out `terms_of_service` from the seed files entirely, which aligns with how the fork migrated to the new terms fields. Let me verify that `terms_of_service` genuinely has no accessor anywhere.

action.command:
cd /workspace && echo "=== custom/user.rb: attr_accessor & terms accessors ==="; grep -n "attr_accessor\|attr_writer\|attr_reader\|terms" app/models/custom/user.rb | head -20; echo "=== confirm: can we set terms_of_service on fresh instance? ==="; export PATH=/usr/local/ruby/bin:$PATH PGPASSWORD=root; timeout 120 bin/rails runner '
u = User.new
begin
  u.terms_of_service = "1"; puts "set terms_of_service OK (accessor exists)"
rescue=>e; puts "set terms_of_service => #{e.class}"
end
' 2>&1 | tail -3
